newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti 1996 pre-tax loss 800 bln lire.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti 1996 pre-tax loss 800 bln lire.

text.p: Italy's information and technology group Olivetti on Wednesday said its pre-tax loss for 1996 was around 800 billion lire while its annual sales fell 16 percent to 8.27 trillion lire from 1995.
In a statement following the company's first board meeting in 1997, Olivetti said that its debt at end-December 1996 was 2.250 trillion lire against 2.916 trillion lire at the end-November.

The Olivetti statement said that the 800 billion lire ($496.5 million) of pretax losses included 200 billion lire of losses from its 35.5 percent owned mobile phone group Omnitel, which Olivetti said said was in line with the company's own forecasts.

The group said that a sale of a 5.6 percent stake in Omnitel and U.S. venture capital stakes had netted 531 billion lire which gave the group a improvement in cash flows of 159 billion lire. Restructuring charges amounted to 24 billion lire.

Olivetti added that its group debt levels could vary as the situation at its 200 companies within the whole Olivetti group were fully assessed, and final figures will be produced in its 1996 consolidated financial statement to be published later.

Group chief executive Roberto Colaninno said in the statement that after the sale of its personal computer company earlier this month, the group had a structure in line with its own strategic plan to focus on telecoms, information technology and office products. ($ = 1611 Italian Lire)
